item.title: 2027: Sowore’s AAC writes Tinubu, demands presidential villa for campaign council inauguration
item.description: By Emmanuel Okogba The African Action Congress (AAC) has formally requested approval from President Bola Tinubu to hold the inauguration of its Presidential Campaign Council at the Presidential Villa in Aso Rock, Abuja, and has asked for logistical support for 5,000 participants. In a letter dated 21 October 2026 and signed by National Secretary Oshiokhue Philip Ikpeminoghena, the party said it wants to stage the ceremony on 11 November 2026 “in preparation for the 2027 general elections.” The AAC also requested the provision of food, drinks and other logistical support for the 5,000 expected attendees from within Nigeria and abroad. The party said the request was made “consistent with the arrangements reportedly extended to the All Progressives Congress (APC) for a similar political engagement.” “In the spirit of multiparty democracy, political inclusiveness, and equal treatment of political parties,” the letter stated, granting the request would demonstrate the Presidency’s commitment to fairness, equal access, and the principle that public institutions must serve all Nigerians without partisan discrimination. The AAC said it looks forward to a favourable response and asked for information on the applicable procedures and conditions for approval. The letter was addressed to the President and Commander-in-Chief at the Presidential Villa, Aso Rock, Abuja. item.title: Netanyahu’s main election rival rules out serving under him
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s main rival in October 27 elections, ex-army chief Gadi Eisenkot, said on Wednesday that he would refuse to serve as a minister in a new government led by the current premier. With the poll just days away, and predictions that no side will win on its own, some commentators have raised the possibility of a unity government convening Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc with centrist and centre-right parties. But speaking to radio station 103 FM on Wednesday, Eisenkot said he was committed, “categorically, to not serving under Netanyahu’s leadership, even within the framework of a rotation” deal in which the two shared power. Eisenkot has campaigned on attacking the fitness to serve of Netanyahu, especially over his failure to prevent the October 7, 2023 attack by Hamas. Polls show Netanyahu’s right-wing coalition and the opposition camp rallying around Eisenkot are neck and neck, with each projected to win around 50 to 52 seats — just shy of a majority in the 120-member Knesset. In his interview, Eisenkot did not rule out the possibility of a unity government altogether. Former prime minister Naftali Bennet, whose party is polling third, said a government that included the current prime minister would not be an issue for him. It would, however, run counter to Israeli law, which forbids anyone facing charges from serving as a minister — although the bar does not apply for prime minister. Netanyahu is currently on trial and faces several charges of corruption, which he denies. An October 16 poll found that 55 percent of respondents would prefer a unity government over new elections should the upcoming vote fail to produce a clear winner. In 2020, Netanyahu and centrist Benny Gantz set aside their mutual antipathy to strike a power-sharing deal in which they would rotate the prime ministership between them. The agreement followed a period that saw three elections in less than a year, and the resulting government lasted only 13 months. Otu explained that the 2027–2029 Medium-Term Expenditure Framework and Fiscal Strategy Paper provided the foundation for the estimates, adding that the budget would sustain ongoing programmes while opening new pathways for investment, employment creation and improved public services. “The imperative of this exercise underscores our collective resolve to chart a sustainable course for the growth and development of our dear State,” he declared. Addressing concerns surrounding the state’s debt profile, the governor maintained that his administration had refrained from obtaining fresh domestic and external loans since assuming office in 2023. Citing verifiable indices from the National Bureau of Statistics and the Debt Management Office, he said Cross River remained among the few states that had not contracted new loans during the period. He attributed the state’s existing debt burden to obligations inherited from previous administrations, explaining that debt servicing had constrained the pace at which available resources could be deployed to development projects. He further clarified that the naira value of external debt had been affected by currency devaluation and foreign-exchange liberalisation. “I cannot, and will never mortgage the future of our children with unsustainable loans,” Otu declared, pledging to strengthen internally generated revenue, maximise federal allocations and attract development assistance and private-sector investment to finance the state’s development priorities. Reviewing the performance of the 2026 budget, the governor acknowledged the pressures of exchange-rate volatility, rising operational costs, supply-chain disruptions and inherited debt obligations. He disclosed that the administration had collaborated with the legislature to enact a supplementary budget, raising the spending framework to ₦963.07 billion to accommodate urgent interventions and counterpart-funding requirements. Among the achievements highlighted was the delivery of more than 608 kilometres of interconnected road projects across the three senatorial districts, including the Nsan–Oban Road in Akamkpa, the Adiabo–Ikoneto Road in Odukpani and the Yahe–Ebo–Wanakade Road in Yala. He also reported progress in rural electrification through solar streetlights, mini-grids and network rehabilitation, describing the interventions as essential to reopening economic corridors, improving mobility and restoring commercial activity in underserved communities. Agriculture featured prominently in the governor’s account of the administration’s economic transformation agenda. Otu disclosed that more than 20,000 bags of fertiliser had been distributed to 8,000 farmers, while over one million improved oil-palm, cowpea and cocoa seedlings had been provided to farmers across the state. He also highlighted the establishment of a 50,000-hectare rice project and support for more than 5,300 livestock farmers, alongside loans, grants and agricultural machinery for smallholder and large-scale producers. According to him, an ₦18 billion offtake arrangement had helped advance the state’s agricultural initiatives, while the cash-crop revolution was strengthening the productive capacity of farmers. “There is no food security without agriculture,” he asserted, adding that the government intended to become Nigeria’s leading cocoa and oil-palm-producing state through expanded cultivation, mechanisation, agro-allied industries and private-sector partnerships. On healthcare, education and public-sector welfare, Otu outlined interventions designed to improve access, strengthen institutions and enhance service delivery. He cited the renovation and rehabilitation of hospitals, the establishment of medical oxygen plants in Calabar and Ogoja in partnership with UNICEF, and the upgrading of state-owned Schools of Nursing and Midwifery to accreditation standards. He also highlighted a reported 95 per cent routine immunisation coverage, implementation of the Consolidated Medical Salary Structure for medical workers and an increase in the retirement age of health workers from 60 to 65 years. item.title: Delta youths seize Macaraba oil field over alleged marginalization
item.description: By Jimitota Onoyume Hundreds of youths from Ifie-Kporo community in Warri South local government area of Delta state yesterday (today Wednesday) shut down operations at the Macaraba oil field, accusing the operating firm of marginalising the community and refusing to recognise it as a host community. The protesters, who arrived at the field in speedboats, demanded justice, youth employment, and recognition of the community’s rights over Wells 24 and 25. They carried placards with several inscriptions which included , “We Want Justice,” “Employ Our Youths,” and “Give Us Our Rights or Leave Our Land.” The youths accused the oil firm of operating on their ancestral land without adequately recognising or engaging the community, vowing to remain at the field until their grievances are addressed. Speaking during the protest, one of the youths, who gave his name as Tosan, said the company had been unfair to the community and warned that the occupation would continue until their demands were met. The protesters insisted that Wells 24 and 25 sit on Ifie-Kporo ancestral land and urged the firm to respect their rights as a host community in line with the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA). They called on the company to follow the precedent set by Gulf, which they said had recognised and engaged with the community as host to its oil facilities. The youths warned that continued neglect of their demands could threaten peace in the area, and urged the firm to resolve the dispute through dialogue rather than allow the situation to escalate. item.title: 5 things to know about Chinese AI startup DeepSeek
item.description: The United States Department of Homeland Security ordered government agencies on Monday to stop using artificial intelligence tools from DeepSeek, citing concerns over data being transferred to China. Here are five things to know about the Chinese AI startup following the new restrictions: – ‘Sputnik moment’ – Founded by Liang Wenfeng in the eastern Chinese tech hub Hangzhou, DeepSeek started life in 2023 as a side project of Liang’s data-driven hedge fund that had access to a cache of powerful AI processors made by US chip giant Nvidia. It gained global attention in January 2025 with the release of its R1 deep-reasoning large language model, which sparked a US tech share sell-off. Industry insiders were stunned by R1’s high performance — at a level similar to ChatGPT and other leading US chatbots — and DeepSeek’s claims to have developed it at a fraction of the cost. Venture capitalist Marc Andreessen described it as a “Sputnik moment”, referencing the 1957 launch of Earth’s first artificial satellite by the Soviet Union that stunned the Western world. – Censorship concerns – Like other Chinese chatbots, DeepSeek’s AI tools eschew topics usually censored in the world’s second-largest economy, such as the 1989 Tiananmen crackdown. That and data privacy concerns have led DeepSeek AI to be banned or restricted on government-issued devices in several countries, including the United States, Australia and South Korea. On Monday, the US went further by banning civilian government agencies from using products developed by DeepSeek and third-party tools created using DeepSeek. China’s foreign ministry said it opposed that move and accused the US of “overstretching” the concept of national security. DeepSeek’s low cost and ease of deployment have made it a popular choice in developing countries, analysts say. The company holds around four percent of global market share for chatbots, according to web traffic analysis company Similarweb. ChatGPT dominates at 68 percent. – Open source – DeepSeek’s systems are open-source, meaning their inner workings are public, allowing programmers to customise parts of the software to suit their needs. item.title: Toulouse v Troyes Ligue 1 game postponed as France gripped by unrest
item.description: The Ligue 1 match between Toulouse and Troyes this weekend has has pushed back a day at the request of local authorities struggling to contain unrest in France, the French league (LFP) announced on Wednesday. The match which had been due to take place in Toulouse in southwest France at 1715 local time (1515 GMT) on Saturday will now kick off on Sunday at the same time. “Although not considered high-risk, organising an event with such a large turnout requires the deployment of internal security forces and municipal police personnel,” the Haute-Garonne prefecture, which manages public services and security in the region, said. A second sporting event is also scheduled in Toulouse on Saturday with the city’s rugby club set to host Perpignan in a Top 14 rugby match. On Tuesday, the Ligue 2 match between Montpellier and Paris-based Red Star originally scheduled for Saturday was moved to Monday. Some of the worst urban violence to hit France in years erupted last Saturday on the fringe of nationwide protests over the rising cost of living. Since then, authorities have ordered partial curfews in parts of Paris and other cities, including Toulouse, to prevent further violence. There was tight security at the Parc des Princes in Paris on Tuesday for Paris Saint-Germain’s victory against Barcelona in the Champions League. item.title: Jonathan urges Nigeria to shift from imports to production
item.description: By Soni Daniel ABUJA — Former President Goodluck Jonathan has called on Nigeria to develop the resources and technology needed to produce goods and services locally rather than continue to depend on imports. Jonathan made the call on Wednesday while commissioning the Zeetin Technologies plant in Idu, Abuja, which manufactures tricycles for the Nigerian market. He said Nigeria’s large youth population could serve as a major asset in boosting local production, creating economic opportunities and driving national development. The former president urged Nigeria to emulate countries that had successfully mobilised their resources and young populations to expand their manufacturing capacity and become reliable producers and exporters of goods. He stressed the need for Nigeria to harness its human and material resources to strengthen domestic production and reduce dependence on imported goods. item.title: Toluwanisings’ family announces service of songs, seeks support for widow, children
item.description: The family of late Nigerian gospel singer Olayemi Bayonle Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings, has announced a night of tributes and service of songs in his honour while appealing to the public for financial support for his wife and children. The event is scheduled for Tuesday, October 27, 2026, at 3pm at the Hall of Grace, Jogor Centre, Ibadan, Oyo State. The family announced the programme in a post on the singer’s social media page, inviting friends, colleagues, fans and well-wishers to celebrate his life and ministry. “We invite you to join us for a Night of Tributes and Service of Songs in honour of our beloved brother, friend, and gospel minister, Olayemi Bayonle Bolaji, fondly known as Toluwanisings,” the statement read. In a separate appeal titled “A Call for Love and Support,” the family urged Nigerians to assist the singer’s wife and children following his death on October 14. The family called on well-meaning individuals to contribute towards supporting the widow as she navigates life after the loss of her husband. “As we mourn the loss of our beloved brother, let us stand with his wife during this difficult season. Every contribution, no matter how small, is a gesture of love and compassion,” the family said. It also provided account details for donations and prayed for blessings on those willing to support the bereaved family. “Please support her through the account details provided. May God bless every giving heart and grant the family strength and comfort,” the statement added. Toluwanisings died on October 14, 2026, hours after ministering at a praise concert organised by fellow gospel singer Bidemi Olaoba in Ibadan. His death sparked widespread reactions on social media, with questions raised about access to emergency medical care after his personal assistant alleged that several hospitals refused to admit him. The planned night of tributes and service of songs will provide an opportunity for family members, friends, colleagues and fans to honour the late singer’s life and musical contributions. item.title: Suspected kidnappers kill 7-year-old boy hours after demanding N2.5m ransom in Jos
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos A seven-year-old boy, Abdullahi Rabi’u, has been found dead hours after suspected kidnappers abducted him and demanded a ransom of N2.5 million in Majema area, along Ring Road, Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State. The victim’s uncle, Sukairaj Danladi Gado, who narrated the incident, said the boy was sent on an errand to a neighbour’s house on Monday evening but failed to return after delivering the message. “The family became worried when Abdullahi did not return home. We made efforts to locate him, but all our efforts proved abortive,” Gado said. He said, “On Tuesday morning, we received a call from an unidentified telephone number. The caller demanded N2.5 million as ransom and informed us that the boy had been kidnapped.” According to him, “We agreed to pay the ransom because we wanted the boy to return home alive. We were hoping that he would be released, but what happened later shattered our hopes.” Gado said, “We were devastated when we received the news that his body had been found. It was a painful experience for the family because we had hoped to secure his release.” He added, “The boy’s body was reportedly discovered on Tuesday evening in a narrow passage near his family’s residence. The incident has thrown the family and residents of the neighbourhood into mourning.” Expressing concern over the killing, the uncle said, “We suspect that the people behind this incident may be familiar with the neighbourhood. We want security agencies to investigate the matter and ensure that those responsible are arrested.” He further said, “We are appealing to the security agencies to do everything possible to unravel the circumstances surrounding his death and bring the perpetrators to justice so that other families will not experience this kind of tragedy.” Efforts to obtain reactions from security operatives were unsuccessful as of press time. item.description: The Senate has called on the Federal Government to provide emergency funding from the service-wide vote to strengthen the country’s disease surveillance system and enforce mandatory health screening at all international airports, seaports and designated land borders to prevent the spread of Ebola and other epidemic-prone diseases. item.title: Ligue 1 game postponed as unrest grips France
item.description: The Ligue 1 match between Toulouse and Troyes this weekend has been pushed back a day at the request of local authorities struggling to contain unrest in France, the French league (LFP) announced on Wednesday. The match, which had been due to take place in Toulouse in southwest France at 1715 local time (1515 GMT) on Saturday, will now kick off on Sunday at the same time. “Although not considered high-risk, organising an event with such a large turnout requires the deployment of internal security forces and municipal police personnel,” the Haute-Garonne prefecture, which manages public services and security in the region, said. A second sporting event is also scheduled in Toulouse on Saturday, with the city’s rugby club set to host Perpignan in a Top 14 rugby match. On Tuesday, the Ligue 2 match between Montpellier and Paris-based Red Star originally scheduled for Saturday was moved to Monday. Some of the worst urban violence to hit France in years erupted last Saturday on the fringe of nationwide protests over the rising cost of living. Since then, authorities have ordered partial curfews in parts of Paris and other cities, including Toulouse, to prevent further violence. There was tight security at the Parc des Princes in Paris on Tuesday for Paris Saint-Germain’s victory against Barcelona in the Champions League. PSG will host Lyon at the same venue in a Ligue 1 match on Sunday evening. AFP The post Ligue 1 game postponed as unrest grips France appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Cross River Assembly passes State Police Bill
item.description: By Ike Uchechukwu, Calabar The Cross River State House of Assembly on Tuesday passed the Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, endorsing the proposed establishment of state police to address insecurity through a decentralised policing system. All 22 lawmakers present at plenary voted in favour of the bill, with none opposing it. Three of the Assembly’s 25 members were absent during the vote. The bill seeks to provide a constitutional framework for the establishment of State Police Services in Nigeria. It contains 26 clauses and proposes 25 alterations through substitutions to provisions of the principal Act, including Sections 84(4), 89(2), 121(3), 124(4), 109(2), 153(1), 157(2), 158(1) and 160. Speaker of the House, Rt. Hon. Elvert Ayambem, said the vote reflected the Assembly’s commitment to constitutional reforms aimed at addressing security challenges and protecting lives and property. “By this vote, the 10th Assembly has demonstrated its support for the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, which seeks to establish a constitutional framework for State Police Services,” he said. Ayambem, however, stressed that the implementation of state policing must be guided by the rule of law, accountability and democratic principles. Contributing to the debate, the Leader of the House and member representing Odukpani State Constituency, Rt. Hon. Francis Asuquo, said policing must be brought closer to the people. He argued that a decentralised system would improve security responses and enable law enforcement agencies to address challenges peculiar to grassroots communities. The member representing Yala I State Constituency, Hon. Brian Odey, called for effective coordination between state and federal security agencies to ensure that the proposed State Police Services complemented existing security structures and improved overall operations. The Deputy Leader of the House and member representing Abi State Constituency, Rt. Hon. Davies Eta, emphasised the need for adequate safeguards, accountability and professionalism in the proposed system. He said state police must operate within the confines of the law and respect citizens’ fundamental rights. Lawmakers also identified improved intelligence gathering and better protection of lives and property as potential benefits of decentralised policing. The passage marks the Cross River Assembly’s endorsement of the proposed constitutional amendments. The bill must proceed through the constitutionally prescribed amendment process before the proposed changes can take effect nationally. item.title: Uganda denies Ebola outbreak after Nigeria confirms imported case
item.description: Uganda has denied having an active Ebola outbreak following Nigeria’s confirmation of an imported case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), insisting that it has no confirmed active infections as authorities investigate where the patient contracted the virus. In a public statement issued in Kampala on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, Uganda’s Ministry of Health said the Nigerian patient had travelled through the country before arriving in Nigeria but stressed that her transit did not establish where she was infected. “We wish to clarify that, as at the time of this statement, Uganda has NO confirmed active Ebola cases,” the ministry said. The statement, titled “Reported Ebola Case in Nigeria: We Call for Calm and Vigilance,” added that preliminary information indicated the woman had travelled through Uganda in early October without symptoms and developed them after arriving in Nigeria. “Travel through Uganda does not establish that infection occurred here. The location of exposure remains under investigation,” the ministry said. It added that Nigeria’s government was expected to provide detailed information about the woman’s travel itinerary and clinical history to support further investigations and any necessary contact tracing. The Ugandan authorities also said they were strengthening screening and public health controls at points of entry in collaboration with relevant agencies. item.title: NBTI announces $600m pipeline for Nigerian innovation
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The National Board for Technology Incubation (NBTI) has unveiled an investment and development-finance pipeline exceeding $600 million for solar energy and other development initiatives, following the participation of 298 Nigerian innovators at the NextGen Innovation Challenge 2026 in London. The proposed financing comprises a $500 million solar-energy programme for universities and polytechnics and a $100 million financing arrangement for the Tinubu Light Initiative. The funds, however, have not been confirmed as received or fully mobilised. Speaking at a world press conference on Wednesday, NBTI Director-General, Dr Kazeem Kolawole Raji, said the October 9 event, organised in partnership with UKALD, provided an international platform for showcasing Nigerian technologies and connecting innovators with investors and commercial partners. The number of participating innovators rose from 105 in 2025 to 298 this year, representing all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, with innovations spanning agriculture, healthcare, artificial intelligence, renewable energy and advanced manufacturing. “Our innovators have demonstrated that Nigeria has ideas worthy of international attention. Our responsibility is to help create the conditions in which those ideas can grow, compete and deliver lasting value to our people,” Raji said. NBTI said discussions with Gigawatt Global focused on developing solar farms in universities and polytechnics under power purchase agreements, while a memorandum of understanding with Financial Innovation for Impact, UK, also known as Cambridge Investors, covered the proposed $100 million financing for the Tinubu Light Initiative. The initiative targets one million micro and small businesses for solar-energy solutions, 50,000 direct youth jobs and 10,000 trained field marketers, with ₦30 billion in blended financing targeted for its first phase. Other outcomes include an announced $100,000 investment commitment by Dubai-based investor Erin Grover for three women innovators and international acceleration opportunities valued at $160,000 for 16 selected innovators. The Learning and Development Bureau UK also offered leadership and management scholarships worth more than £80,000 collectively to the 16 innovators and pledged assistance with UK Global Talent Visa applications, subject to eligibility. Raji said the priority was now to turn the opportunities into viable businesses, jobs and measurable economic benefits, urging investors and development partners to support Nigerian innovators with funding, mentorship and market access. “Our focus must now move decisively from visibility to implementation, from promising concepts to commercially viable solutions, and from announcements to independently verifiable outcomes,” he said. item.title: PANDEF mourns Uduaghan, hails his peacebuilding role
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF), the apex socio-political body of the South-South geopolitical zone, has mourned the death of former Delta State Governor, Dr Emmanuel Uduaghan, who died three days before his 72nd birthday, according to his family. PANDEF National Chairman, Ambassador Godknows Igali, described Uduaghan as an exceptional leader whose commitment to the people of Delta State was unwavering. Igali stated this in a condolence letter to Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, on the death of the former governor, according to a statement issued on Wednesday. He praised Uduaghan for his significant contributions to peace and stability in the Niger Delta, particularly during his tenure as Secretary to the State Government and later as governor, when militancy was heightened across the region. In the letter, Igali said he was shocked by the news of Uduaghan’s death, describing the late governor as a close associate and personal friend. “I write to express my total shock at the news of the passing into glory of our dearly beloved brother, the former Governor of Delta State, HE Dr Emmanuel Uduaghan. Although we mourn, but we all hold strong belief that the Almighty God knows best, and we glorify His exalted name,” he said. Igali added that he and Uduaghan had maintained a cordial relationship since they served simultaneously as secretaries to their respective state governments. “Without doubt, he was an exceptional man through and through, whose commitment to the people of Delta State was unfettered,” he said. He noted that Uduaghan played a significant role in bringing peace and stability to the Niger Delta during a period of heightened militancy in the South-South region. Igali described the former governor’s death as a major loss not only to Delta State but also to the Niger Delta and Nigeria as a whole. He expressed hope that Uduaghan’s legacy of service to God and humanity would endure, saying the late governor had “embedded his name in gold in the annals of our history.” Igali also asked Oborevwori to convey his deepest condolences to the Uduaghan family and the people of Delta State, praying for the repose of the former governor’s soul. He also cautioned political actors against actions capable of undermining national stability, particularly the premature or unauthorised announcement of election results in ways that could trigger political tension and plunge the country into chaos. “The scar in my heart from the loss of Chief Moshood Kashimawo Olawale Abiola has not fully healed,” Showunmi said, adding that he would neither trivialise Abiola’s sacrifice nor pretend to be unfamiliar with the painful experiences that shaped Nigeria’s democratic struggle. He stressed that his remarks on the country’s political history had been misunderstood by some people, insisting that his intention was to caution against political conduct that could endanger peace, violate the law or destabilise the nation. Showunmi said his reference to the political events of 1992 was intended to illustrate the consequences of abandoning caution, restraint and respect for the law in the pursuit of political power. “I invoked the events of 1992 to illustrate how political situations can spiral out of control when caution, restraint and respect for the law are abandoned,” he said. He maintained that his intervention was intended as a warning about the potential consequences of political decisions, not an endorsement of reckless conduct. “My intervention was a warning about consequences, not an invitation to recklessness, and I will not permit reactionary forces to turn my counsel into something it was never intended to be,” he stated. According to him, political advice should be offered in the national interest, while individuals must ultimately decide whether to heed such counsel. He urged political contestants to consider the wider implications of their actions, warning that decisions taken without regard for the law and national stability could have far-reaching consequences for the country. Reaffirming his commitment to national unity, Showunmi declared that his political convictions were not driven by ethnic considerations and rejected any suggestion that he subscribed to the superiority of one ethnic group over another. “I must also state, unequivocally, that I am a Pan-Nigerian through and through. I have no interest in promoting the idea that one ethnic group is superior to another,” he said. He explained that his political philosophy was rooted in the collective dignity, security and prosperity of Nigerians, irrespective of their ethnic or regional backgrounds. Showunmi urged Yoruba activists and others who might disagree with his position to consider his statements within the broader context of his commitment to Nigeria’s unity. “My words and actions must be understood within the framework of my commitment to the Nigerian nation. I will not subordinate that commitment to ethnic sentiment, sectional advantage or the politics of exclusion,” he said. He added that his preference for national cohesion should not be interpreted as a lack of personal conviction or an inadequate understanding of the country’s political history. On Nigeria’s political future, Showunmi reiterated his support for a power-sharing arrangement under which the presidency would rotate between the northern and southern parts of the country. He argued that a predictable and mutually respected understanding of power rotation could help reduce political suspicion, strengthen national cohesion and promote democratic stability. “I have long expressed the view that Nigeria should manage political power through a pendulum arrangement between the Northern and Southern parts of the country,” he said. “In my considered opinion, a predictable and mutually respected understanding of power rotation offers a framework for reducing suspicion, strengthening national cohesion and sustaining our democratic journey.” He described the proposal as part of the broader need for political maturity, mutual understanding and an inclusive approach to managing Nigeria’s diversity. Paying tribute to Abiola, the presumed winner of the June 12, 1993 presidential election, which was annulled by the military government, Showunmi said the late politician’s legacy remained inseparable from Nigeria’s struggle for democratic governance. He prayed that Abiola’s sacrifice would continue to inspire Nigerians to work towards a more stable, just and enduring democracy. “May your supreme sacrifice continue to guide Nigeria towards a more stable, just and enduring democracy. May the promise for which you paid such a terrible price never be betrayed,” he said. Showunmi also disclosed that he intended to speak more extensively in the future about his personal contributions to the pro-democracy struggle and how the events surrounding Abiola shaped his political trajectory. “One day, God willing, I will speak more fully about my own contributions to the struggle for democracy,” he said. According to him, the experiences surrounding Abiola and the struggle to reclaim the June 12 mandate influenced his political outlook and redirected the course of his life, setting in motion developments whose consequences he said were still unfolding. He also acknowledged the role played by media entrepreneur and publisher Dele Momodu during that period, describing his contribution as significant to that chapter of Nigeria’s political history. “I must also acknowledge Dele Momodu. May God spare his life. He played a key and pivotal role in that chapter of our history, and his contribution deserves to be remembered,” Showunmi said. Showunmi warned against interpreting his restraint as a lack of knowledge of Nigeria’s democratic history or mistaking his commitment to national unity for an absence of personal convictions. “Finally, let nobody mistake my restraint for ignorance of history or my commitment to national unity for an absence of personal conviction,” he said. He added: “My commitment is to Nigeria. My loyalty is to the democratic ideal. My respect for MKO Abiola’s sacrifice is enduring. And my conviction that Nigeria must survive, mature and prosper remains unshaken.” “May God bless Nigeria and all who genuinely labour for her progress,” he said. item.title: Reps Call For Early Isolation Camp Preparations To Prevent Ebola Spread
item.description: The House of Representatives on Wednesday called for increased public awareness as well as early preparation of isolation camps following confirmation of a fresh outbreak in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). During a session on Wednesday, Reps members also called for alertness and asked the Federal Government to take advantage of the 2014 blueprint with which the Ebola virus was contained. The committee on infectious disease has been mandated to immediately swing into action to ensure that the resolutions of the House are promptly carried out. According to the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate, the imported case of Ebola virus disease was confirmed by laboratory testing. Health workers attend a training by medical charity, Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF), to reinforce regional emergency response capacity for Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) at Ongata Rongai, Kajiado County in Kenya on July 10, 2026. Speaking at a media briefing in Abuja, Pate said the patient is a woman with a recent travel history to East Africa, particularly Uganda, who returned to Nigeria with symptoms on October 7th, which progressed four days later before tests confirmed the infection. He said the patient is currently in isolation and receiving medical care, and contact tracing has commenced, with forty-four contacts already identified, as surveillance is strengthened at the country’s entry points. “The patient, a woman who recently arrived in Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda, was admitted to a private hospital… where she received care for several days before the diagnosis was confirmed,” a government statement said. “She is currently in isolation and receiving medical care.” The Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate. Pate explained that the Ministry of Health, the FCT Health Secretariat, the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, and other partners are working together to contain the infection and prevent further spread. While urging public and private health facilities to remain on high alert, stressing that health workers must maintain a high index of suspicion for possible cases, he called on Nigerians to remain calm and vigilant. The minister advised the public to practise good hygiene, watch out for symptoms including fever, weakness, headache and diarrhoea, and cooperate with public health officials. He maintained that the situation is being managed, with the government pledging timely and transparent updates as efforts continue to contain the virus. Ebola spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person, or with contaminated materials. Symptoms can include fever, headache, severe weakness, vomiting and diarrhoea. The post Reps Call For Early Isolation Camp Preparations To Prevent Ebola Spread appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: PSG’s Kvaratskhelia Set For Long Absence With Torn ACL
item.description: Paris Saint-Germain winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia requires surgery after tearing his ACL in the Champions League win against Barcelona, the European champions, said on Wednesday. “Having suffered a torn anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee during yesterday’s match against FC Barcelona, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia is set to undergo surgery in the coming days,” PSG said in a statement. PSG’s Georgian forward Khvicha Kvaratskhelia lies on the pitch after sustaining an injury during the UEFA Champions League first round day 3 football match between Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) and FC Barcelona at the Parc des Princes stadium in Paris on October 20, 2026. (Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP) In more bad news for PSG, the club said forward Ousmane Dembele and central defender Marquinhos will both be sidelined for “several weeks” with injuries. Kvaratskhelia slumped to the turf without any apparent contact and left the pitch just before the hour mark in the 4-2 league phase victory against Barcelona at the Parc des Princes on Tuesday. The 25-year-old Georgia international played a leading role in helping PSG to win back-to-back Champions League titles and is one of the contenders for the Ballon d’Or, which will be awarded on Monday. Dembele, the current Ballon d’Or holder, and Marquinhos both suffered thigh injuries, PSG said. Vitinha’s superb late strike proved crucial as reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain saw off rivals Barcelona 4-2 on Tuesday in a dramatic game between two of the leading contenders to win this season’s Champions League. The match was poised at 2-2 when the Portuguese playmaker, who came third in last year’s Ballon d’Or ranking, controlled on his chest and fired in from just outside the box in the 81st minute at the Parc des Princes. Fabian Ruiz then sealed PSG’s third victory in as many outings in this season’s competition, as they aim to win the Champions League for the third season running. item.title: Ebola: Is Nigeria ready?
item.description: T he confirmation of an Ebola case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja, has renewed concerns about Nigeria’s preparedness for a disease that once threatened to overwhelm parts of the country’s health system. In a statement on Tuesday, Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, confirmed that a woman who recently arrived in Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda had tested positive for Ebola after receiving treatment at a private hospital in Abuja. According to the minister, the woman is currently in isolation and receiving medical care. Authorities have identified 44 close contacts and commenced contact tracing to establish whether the patient may have exposed other people to the virus before her diagnosis. The Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), the FCT Health Services Secretariat and other relevant agencies are coordinating the response. Nigeria’s Ebola Outbreak Explained Nigeria’s experience with Ebola Nigeria’s experience with Ebola in 2014 demonstrated how quickly an imported infection could become a national public health emergency in a country with a large population and busy international travel routes. On July 20, 2014, Patrick Sawyer, a Liberian-American diplomat who was infected with Ebola, arrived at Murtala Muhammed International Airport in Lagos from Liberia. He was subsequently admitted to a private hospital, where his illness was initially difficult to distinguish from other diseases. He died on July 25, 2014. His arrival triggered an emergency response involving the Federal Ministry of Health, the Lagos State Government, the NCDC and international health partners. According to a report published in the United States Centres for Disease Control and Prevention’s Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report, Nigeria recorded 20 Ebola cases, comprising 19 laboratory-confirmed cases and one probable case, by September 24, 2014. Eight fatalities from seven laboratory-confirmed Ebola and one probable case were recorded. The deaths included Sawyer and Dr Ameyo Stella Adadevoh, who placed the foreigner in quarantine, as well as six others who were infected during the chain of transmission that followed his arrival. The outbreak was eventually contained, with no new cases reported after August 31, 2014. The country identified and monitored 894 contacts during the response, while 11 patients with laboratory-confirmed Ebola were discharged from care. How prepared is the country for Ebola? Nigeria’s latest preparedness efforts began before the reported FCT case. On June 9, 2026, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu approved the immediate release of N10 billion as emergency intervention funding for public health preparedness and response. The fund is separate from a N21.2 million per-state disbursement under the State Outbreak Investigation and Response Fund. The Presidency also announced the establishment of a Presidential Task Force on Ebola Virus Disease Preparedness and Emerging Public Health Threats, chaired by the Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila. According to the State House, the fund was intended to strengthen the operational capacity of the NCDC and support critical national public health emergency response activities. The government also directed states hosting international airports and international border corridors, alongside relevant ministries, departments and agencies, to submit their preparedness plans, funding requirements and intervention needs. The measures announced included intensified passenger screening at international airports, enhanced monitoring of passengers arriving through designated high-risk routes, and the activation of referral and isolation centres at the Lagos and Abuja international airports. Other proposed measures included health declaration systems for passengers arriving from or transiting through designated high-risk countries and improved coordination among health, immigration, aviation and security authorities. The funding decision followed warnings about the possibility of Ebola being imported into Nigeria as outbreaks emerged in Central Africa. In a May 28, 2026, advisory, the NCDC assessed Nigeria’s risk of importation as high, citing regional transmission, international travel, population movement, porous land borders and the difficulty of distinguishing early Ebola symptoms from common illnesses such as malaria and Lassa fever. The agency said preparedness needed to cover every state and the FCT, with emphasis on early detection, isolation, laboratory diagnosis, infection prevention and control, contact tracing and the protection of healthcare workers. Daily Trust reported in September that three months later, there was no public breakdown of how the N10 billion was spent, as checks at airports and isolation facilities revealed the presence of the preparedness gap the money was meant to close. They didn’t check my provisional sign or QR code, and they didn’t check my temperature. They didn’t do any of that. For me, it was almost a waste of time filling out the form,” one of them, Habeebat Ajayi, had told our correspondent.
